title: Senate Agriculture Committee advances Agricultural Act of 2026 from committee
text:
Senate Agriculture Committee advances Agricultural Act of 2026 from committee
The Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry advanced the Agricultural Act of 2026 out of committee on Sep. 16.
The legislation is intended to complement the bipartisan Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which was led by House Committee on Agriculture Chairman Glenn “GT” Thompson and passed out of the House of Representatives in April.
Chairman Glenn “GT” Thompson said, “Advancing the Agricultural Act of 2026 from committee is a significant step in the right direction as we work to restore certainty and common sense to agricultural policy. Farm country cannot wait any longer for updated policies, and I applaud Chairman Boozman and Senate Republicans for recognizing this urgency, even as Senate Democrats refuse to come to the table to support American producers. Passing a full, five-year farm bill remains my top priority, and I look forward to working with any lawmakers who make good faith efforts to support our producers in the coming months.”
The House Committee on Agriculture supports nutrition programs aimed at enhancing access to nutritious foods; it has received recognition for its oversight in financial regulations benefiting agriculture; aligns with Republican members of the U.S. House; supervises federal initiatives fostering innovation within production agriculture; addresses agricultural concerns across multiple states; and influences legislation by shaping farm bills that support climate-smart solutions for farmers and ranchers, according to the official website.
Next steps will involve further consideration by lawmakers as both chambers seek agreement on a final version of a comprehensive five-year farm bill.
